channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: With No Jobs, Remittances Become Lifeline For Afghan Households
item.description: Since the Taliban regained control of Afghanistan five years ago as international military forces withdrew, the country's economy has sputtered, inflation has spiked, and international investment has all but dried up, leaving ordinary Afghans reliant on remittances from abroad to survive With No Jobs, Remittances Become Lifeline For Afghan Households.

item.title: Thailand mulls suspending nearly 6,000 officials over exam scandal
item.description: The scandal began in June, when investigators said they had concluded that officials accepted bribes of up to 800,000 baht (US$23,847) to electronically alter candidates' results to allow them to pass mandatory exams for government appointments or promotions. Thailand mulls suspending nearly 6,000 officials over exam scandal.

item.title: 'Real Work Is The Planning': How Ukrainian Drones Are Striking So Deep Into Russia
item.description: Ukraine is expanding its use of medium-range drones to strike Russian military targets deep behind the front lines. Operators of FP-2 drones told RFE/RL the attacks hit air defenses, troop positions, and logistics hubs, forcing Russia to divert resources to protect sites deep inside its territory. 'Real Work Is The Planning': How Ukrainian Drones Are Striking So Deep Into Russia.

item.title: Moroccan intelligence insider reveals widespread use of Pegasus hacking software
item.description: Whistleblower suggests internal security services deployed spyware from 2017 against key domestic and foreign targetsA former member of Morocco’s domestic intelligence service has helped to provide an unprecedented insight into how the north African state used hacking software – including Pegasus spyware – to target journalists, human rights defenders, French politicians and Spanish cabinet minist Moroccan intelligence insider reveals widespread use of Pegasus hacking software.

But it fits a disturbing pattern that runs through the movement’s entire governing structure: Non-Pashtun commanders are useful until their independence becomes a threat. item.title: Fears for New Zealand’s native species as first bird flu case emerges
item.description: Minister urges public to report cases of three or more sick or dead birds in a group after brown skua seabird tests positive for H5N1 on Wellington beachThe deadly H5N1 bird flu has been confirmed in New Zealand for the first time, sparking alarm that some of the country’s most beloved and vulnerable native birds could be wiped out if it spreads.

item.title: Mexico asks US state attorneys general to investigate immigrant ICE deaths
item.description: Since start of Trump’s second term, 14 Mexican immigrants have died in ICE custody and three in agency operationsMexico formally requested that US state attorneys general criminally investigate cases of immigrants who have died in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody or during raids, the Mexican government said Tuesday. The request follows the death of Mexican immigrant Lorenzo Salgado Arauj Mexico asks US state attorneys general to investigate immigrant ICE deaths.

item.title: The Shadowy Iranian Judge Sending Protesters To Their Death
item.description: Iran has executed some 40 political prisoners since mass protests rocked the country in January. Twelve more may be about to join them, and they were all put on death row by one man: Mohammad Reza Tavakoli, honored by the judiciary as an “exemplary judge.” The Shadowy Iranian Judge Sending Protesters To Their Death.

item.title: US Strikes Target Iranian Ports, Continues Shipping Blockade
item.description: A new round of US strikes across Iran hit dozens of military targets in areas near the Strait of Hormuz, including missile storage and launch sites on Greater Tunb island, according to western military officials. US Strikes Target Iranian Ports, Continues Shipping Blockade.

item.title: New guidance offers hope for reducing the global toll of dementia
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued updated global guidelines aimed at reducing the risk of cognitive decline and dementia, saying that up to 45 per cent of cases may be preventable or delayed by addressing modifiable risk factors throughout life. New guidance offers hope for reducing the global toll of dementia.

item.title: 'Eventually They'll Return To The Table': Middle East Expert Gause Sees Diplomacy Surviving US-Iran
item.description: Despite renewed US strikes on Iran and attacks around the Gulf, veteran Middle East scholar Francis Gregory Gause argues that diplomacy is still alive, and that both Washington and Tehran are once again maneuvering to strengthen their positions before an eventual return to negotiations. 'Eventually They'll Return To The Table': Middle East Expert Gause Sees Diplomacy Surviving US-Iran.

item.title: Why Asia’s AI investment is outpacing AI outcomes
item.description: AI has become one of the few technologies in recent memory that organizations are simultaneously overestimating and underpreparing for. Across Asia-Pacific, investment levels suggest extraordinary confidence in AI’s ability to reshape enterprise performance. The organizational foundations required to realize that value tell a rather different story. KPMG’s inaugural Global AI Pulse survey, publish Why Asia’s AI investment is outpacing AI outcomes.

item.title: US Senate Unveils Revised Russia Sanctions Bill As Lawmakers Push To Cement Graham's Legacy
item.description: A bipartisan group of US senators on July 14 introduced the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026, unveiling a revised package of sanctions and tariffs aimed at squeezing Moscow's war finances while seeking to overcome concerns that had stalled earlier versions of the legislation. US Senate Unveils Revised Russia Sanctions Bill As Lawmakers Push To Cement Graham's Legacy.

item.title: After Double Amputation, Ukrainian Vet Says 'Thirst For Independence' Led The Way To Recovery
item.description: Ukrainian soldier Artem lost both his arms in combat near Pokrovske, a frontline village in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. Recovering from his injuries has meant relearning how to do daily activities -- from getting dressed to working at a computer. After Double Amputation, Ukrainian Vet Says 'Thirst For Independence' Led The Way To Recovery.

item.title: Why The US-Iran Conflict Keeps Shifting Between Fighting And Diplomacy
item.description: As the US and Iran exchange new strikes, military analyst Jonathan Schroden explains why wars often become more violent before peace, how the Strait of Hormuz has become the conflict's strategic centre, and why drones are reshaping naval warfare. Why The US-Iran Conflict Keeps Shifting Between Fighting And Diplomacy.
